symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN cannot reach each other and users report 'duplicate IP address' Windows popups.
topology_note: SW1 (VLAN 10, 192.168.10.0/24) connects PC-A (Fa0/1) and PC-B (Fa0/2). Both PCs were statically configured.
show_outputs:
PC-A: 192.168.10.5/24 | PC-B: 192.168.10.5/24
SW1# show ip arp
Internet  192.168.10.5   -   aabb.cc00.0100  ARPA  Vlan10
Internet  192.168.10.5   -   aabb.cc00.0200  ARPA  Vlan10
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address assigned to PC-A and PC-B

symptom: PC-C can ping its default gateway but cannot reach any other subnet.
topology_note: PC-C is on VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/24) connected to SW2, routed by R1 sub-interface Gi0/0.20.
show_outputs:
PC-C: IP 192.168.20.50 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 192.168.20.1
R1# show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0.20  192.168.20.1  YES manual up  up
expected_fault: Missing route on R1 for other VLAN subnets (no routing protocol or static route configured)

symptom: New host on VLAN 30 cannot communicate with any device, even devices in the same VLAN.
topology_note: PC-D configured with 192.168.30.10/25 while the rest of VLAN 30 uses /24.
expected_fault: Wrong subnet mask configured on PC-D (should be /24, is /25)

symptom: PC-E can ping local subnet devices but not the internet or remote subnets.
topology_note: PC-E gateway configured as 192.168.40.254 but the router interface is 192.168.40.1.
show_outputs:
PC-E: IP 192.168.40.20 Gateway 192.168.40.254
R2# show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/1  192.168.40.1  YES manual up  up
expected_fault: Gateway mismatch - PC-E points to 192.168.40.254 instead of the router's actual IP 192.168.40.1

symptom: All devices connected to switch port Fa0/5 have no network connectivity.
topology_note: SW3 Fa0/5 connects to the access layer switch uplink.
show_outputs:
SW3# show interfaces Fa0/5 status
Port   Name  Status       Vlan  Duplex  Speed
Fa0/5        disabled     10    auto    auto
expected_fault: Interface Fa0/5 administratively down (shutdown)

symptom: Phones on VLAN 50 (voice VLAN) cannot get IP addresses via DHCP.
topology_note: SW4 access port Fa0/10 configured with data VLAN 10 only, no voice VLAN command applied.
show_outputs:
SW4# show interfaces Fa0/10 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (DATA)
Voice VLAN: none
expected_fault: Missing VLAN - voice VLAN 50 not configured on the access port

symptom: Trunk link between SW5 and SW6 is up but VLAN 60 traffic does not pass across it.
topology_note: SW5 Gi0/1 trunk allows VLANs 1,10,20,30,40,50. VLAN 60 was recently added.
show_outputs:
SW5# show interfaces trunk
Port  Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1 1,10,20,30,40,50
expected_fault: Missing VLAN 60 in the trunk allowed list on SW5 Gi0/1

symptom: Branch office PCs cannot reach headquarters subnet 10.1.1.0/24.
topology_note: Branch router R3 has no route toward HQ subnet; static routing is used in this topology.
show_outputs:
R3# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C  192.168.50.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
expected_fault: Missing static route to 10.1.1.0/24 on R3

symptom: PC-F receives an IP address from the wrong subnet (169.254.x.x, APIPA).
topology_note: PC-F is on VLAN 70, DHCP server is centralized and reachable via R4.
show_outputs:
PC-F: IP 169.254.13.44 Mask 255.255.0.0
R4# show run interface Gi0/0.70
no ip helper-address configured
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 70 sub-interface, DHCP requests not relayed

symptom: Users can browse by IP address but websites do not load by name.
topology_note: PC-G configured manually with an incorrect DNS server address.
show_outputs:
PC-G: DNS Server 8.8.4.4.1 (invalid format)
ping 8.8.8.8 succeeds
nslookup google.com times out
expected_fault: Incorrect/invalid DNS server IP configured on PC-G

symptom: Internal hosts cannot reach the internet even though the router has a valid default route.
topology_note: R5 provides internet access via NAT overload on Gi0/0 (outside).
show_outputs:
R5# show ip nat translations
(no translations)
R5# show run | include ip nat
(no ip nat inside/outside statements found)
expected_fault: NAT not configured (missing 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' and NAT overload statement)

symptom: Server 192.168.60.10 is unreachable from an external partner network, though it works from internal hosts.
topology_note: R6 has an ACL applied to Gi0/1 (WAN) inbound to restrict traffic.
show_outputs:
R6# show access-lists
Extended IP access list WAN-IN
 10 deny ip any host 192.168.60.10
 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL entry explicitly denies traffic to server 192.168.60.10

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address.
topology_note: WLC manages AP1; wireless VLAN 80 is mapped to a dynamic interface.
show_outputs:
WLC# show interface summary
Interface Name   VLAN   IP Address
wireless-80      80     0.0.0.0 (not configured)
expected_fault: Wireless dynamic interface VLAN 80 has no IP address / DHCP scope configured

symptom: Wireless clients frequently disconnect and roam poorly between AP1 and AP2.
topology_note: AP1 and AP2 both broadcast SSID 'Corp-WiFi' but on overlapping channels 6 and 6.
show_outputs:
AP1: Channel 6, Power 5
AP2: Channel 6, Power 5
RF report shows high co-channel interference
expected_fault: Channel overlap between AP1 and AP2 causing interference

symptom: Two switches connected via redundant links experience a network-wide broadcast storm.
topology_note: SW7 and SW8 are connected by two links; STP was disabled during a maintenance window.
show_outputs:
SW7# show spanning-tree summary
Spanning tree enabled protocol ieee -- disabled on VLAN 10
expected_fault: Spanning Tree Protocol disabled on VLAN 10, causing a Layer 2 loop

symptom: OSPF neighbors between R7 and R8 never reach FULL state, stuck at 2-WAY.
topology_note: R7 and R8 are on a shared Ethernet segment configured as OSPF area 0.
show_outputs:
R7# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  State      Interface
10.0.0.8    2WAY/DROTHER  Gi0/0
No DR/BDR elected on segment
expected_fault: OSPF DR/BDR election failure, likely due to interface priority set to 0 on both routers

symptom: EIGRP routes to remote site disappear intermittently.
topology_note: R9 and R10 are EIGRP neighbors over a WAN link with a mismatched K-value causing instability.
show_outputs:
R9# show ip eigrp neighbors
(neighbor list empty, flapping)
%DUAL-5-NBRCHANGE: EIGRP-IPv4 Neighbor down
expected_fault: EIGRP K-value mismatch between R9 and R10 preventing stable adjacency

symptom: PC-H on VLAN 90 gets an IP address but cannot ping its own default gateway.
topology_note: SW9 access port Fa0/15 assigned to VLAN 90, but VLAN 90 does not exist in the VLAN database.
show_outputs:
SW9# show vlan brief
(VLAN 90 not listed)
SW9# show interfaces Fa0/15 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 90 (Inactive)
expected_fault: Missing VLAN - VLAN 90 not created in the switch VLAN database

symptom: Remote users report the site-to-site VPN tunnel is down between HQ and branch.
topology_note: R11 (HQ) and R12 (Branch) use an IPsec tunnel over the internet.
show_outputs:
R11# show crypto isakmp sa
dst             src            state     conn-id
(empty - no active SAs)
expected_fault: IPsec Phase 1 (ISAKMP) negotiation failing, likely mismatched pre-shared key

symptom: Users on VLAN 100 can reach internal servers but not the printer on VLAN 100 itself.
topology_note: Printer configured with static IP 192.168.100.99/24, same subnet as users.
show_outputs:
Printer: IP 192.168.100.99 Mask 255.255.255.0
SW10# show ip arp
(no ARP entry learned for 192.168.100.99)
SW10# show interfaces Fa0/20 status
Fa0/20  notconnect  100  auto  auto
expected_fault: Interface down - printer's switch port Fa0/20 shows notconnect (cable/port issue)

symptom: Two servers in the data center both respond to ARP requests for the same IP, causing intermittent connectivity.
topology_note: Server-A and Server-B were both configured with 10.10.10.5 during a migration.
show_outputs:
Core-SW# show ip arp
Internet 10.10.10.5  -  0011.2233.4455 ARPA Vlan200
Internet 10.10.10.5  -  0011.2233.9999 ARPA Vlan200 (flapping)
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address between Server-A and Server-B

symptom: Newly added subnet 172.16.5.0/24 cannot reach the rest of the network despite the router interface being up.
topology_note: R13 interface Gi0/2 is up/up on the new subnet, but no routing protocol advertises it.
show_outputs:
R13# show ip protocols
Routing Protocol is 'ospf 1'
Routing for Networks: 172.16.0.0/16 not listed
R13# show run interface Gi0/2
ip address 172.16.5.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: Missing route/network statement - subnet 172.16.5.0/24 not included in OSPF network statements

symptom: Users report that pings to the gateway work, but web browsing is very slow and times out often.
topology_note: R14 has an access-list applied that unintentionally blocks TCP port 80/443 for a subnet.
show_outputs:
R14# show access-lists WEB-FILTER
10 deny tcp any any eq 80
20 deny tcp any any eq 443
30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL blocking HTTP/HTTPS traffic (ports 80 and 443) for the subnet

symptom: PC-I is configured with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.192 while the rest of VLAN 110 uses 255.255.255.0, causing it to be unable to reach some local peers.
topology_note: VLAN 110 subnet is 192.168.110.0/24; PC-I mistakenly got a /26 mask during manual setup.
expected_fault: Wrong subnet mask on PC-I (/26 instead of /24)

symptom: Guest wireless users can connect but see no internet access, while corporate wireless works fine.
topology_note: Guest VLAN 120 is mapped on the WLC but the uplink trunk to the core switch does not carry VLAN 120.
show_outputs:
Core-SW# show interfaces trunk
Port  Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi1/0/1  1,10,80,90,100,110
expected_fault: Missing VLAN - Guest VLAN 120 not allowed on the trunk to the WLC uplink

symptom: PC-J cannot reach the DHCP server and manually configuring an IP works fine, but auto-config fails.
topology_note: PC-J is on VLAN 130, DHCP server is local (same subnet) so no relay is needed.
show_outputs:
SW11# show interfaces Fa0/25 status
Fa0/25  disabled  130  auto  auto
Port administratively shut down
expected_fault: Interface Fa0/25 administratively down, blocking DHCP broadcast to reach the server

symptom: Remote branch cannot resolve internal hostnames although external DNS resolution works fine.
topology_note: Branch router R15 forwards DNS to public DNS only; internal DNS server 10.1.1.53 is not configured.
show_outputs:
R15# show run | include name-server
ip name-server 8.8.8.8
(internal DNS 10.1.1.53 missing)
expected_fault: Internal DNS server not configured/forwarded, only public DNS is set

symptom: Internet access works for most internal hosts but fails specifically for the 192.168.70.0/24 subnet.
topology_note: R16 performs NAT overload; the NAT ACL only matches some internal subnets.
show_outputs:
R16# show run | include access-list 1
access-list 1 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
access-list 1 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
(192.168.70.0/24 not included)
expected_fault: NAT ACL missing the 192.168.70.0/24 subnet, so it is not translated

symptom: A newly deployed router at the branch cannot reach headquarters even though the WAN link shows up/up.
topology_note: Branch router R17 static default route points to an incorrect next-hop IP typo'd during configuration.
show_outputs:
R17# show ip route
S*  0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.99
Actual ISP next hop should be 203.0.113.9
expected_fault: Gateway mismatch - static default route next-hop IP is mistyped (203.0.113.99 vs correct 203.0.113.9)

symptom: Video calls over Wi-Fi frequently freeze and drop for users near the edge of the building.
topology_note: AP3 covering the far end of the building is set to very low transmit power relative to its coverage area.
show_outputs:
AP3: Tx Power Level 8 (lowest)
Client RSSI values reported around -82 dBm (poor)
expected_fault: AP3 transmit power set too low for required coverage, causing weak signal and drops
